title: 01 · Primitives & dimensions
explanation: Positive technology and labor; unit domestic iceberg costs. Rows always denote importers n and columns exporters i.

title: 02 · Delivered unit costs
explanation: One wage per exporter scales its production cost, then bilateral iceberg costs determine the delivered cost.

title: 03 · Trade shares
equation: pi[n,i] = T[i] c[n,i]^(-theta) / sum_k T[k] c[n,k]^(-theta)
explanation: Normalize competitiveness within each importer row. Log-sum-exp evaluates the denominator without directly raising costs to large negative powers.

title: 04 · Price indices
explanation: The same denominator determines prices. gamma is a fixed positive multiplier and cancels from price changes.

title: 05 · Market clearing
explanation: Transpose the share matrix to sum importer spending into each exporter's sales. This returns all N normalized residuals.

title: 06 · Levels entry point
equation: unit wages → fixed-damping wage iteration → final economic objects
explanation: The levels route supplies its own shares, prices and incomes. The shared wage loop starts at unit wages and retains the final evaluated state.

title: 07 · Explicit iteration loop
equation: evaluate → full residual check → simultaneous wage update → normalize → repeat
explanation: Every evaluated state is recorded. The loop stops only when the full residual is below the target, the update limit is reached, or the numerical state is invalid. Defaults: damping 0.2, target 1e-13, maximum 10,000 updates.

title: 08 · Damping & normalization
explanation: Excess sales relative to income push an exporter's wage up before normalization. Fixed damping takes a fractional log adjustment; subtracting country 0's new log wage fixes the nominal scale after every simultaneous update.

title: 01 · Baseline statistics & shock
explanation: Require a valid, converged baseline and positive trade-cost ratios. The resulting level costs must still be admissible iceberg costs.

title: 02 · Counterfactual shares
equation: a[n,i] = pi0[n,i] (w_hat[i] d_hat[n,i])^(-theta); pi1[n,i] = a[n,i]/sum_k a[n,k]
explanation: Reweight baseline shares using wage and trade-cost changes. This route does not recompute levels competitiveness from technology.

title: 03 · Price changes
explanation: The exponent applies to the whole row sum. gamma cancels because it is held fixed across equilibria.

title: 04 · Hat-market residual
explanation: Labor is fixed, so wage hats scale baseline incomes. The shared loop uses these counterfactual incomes and shares to compute every exporter's sales and residual.

title: 05 · Hat equilibrium solver
explanation: Start from unit wage hats and use the same explicit fixed-damping update. Counterfactual shares and incomes are independently computed from baseline statistics; nothing is copied from the counterfactual levels solution.

title: 06 · Full convergence check
equation: finite positive state AND max_i |r[i]| < 1e-13 → converged
explanation: Every country participates in the residual check, including country 0. Small wage changes alone are not a stopping rule. Limits and invalid numerical states return explicit failure statuses.

title: 01 · Fix the experiment
explanation: The proportional cut is symmetric although initial bilateral costs are asymmetric. All other primitives are held fixed.

title: 02 · Solve E0 and E1
explanation: Both levels runs begin from unit wages. Their difference is entirely the pre-specified trade-cost shock.

title: 03 · Solve hats from E0
explanation: The same shock reaches the independent route through E0's expenditure shares and incomes.

title: 04 · Compare normalized changes
equation: E1/E0 versus hats, under w0[0] = w1[0] = w_hat[0] = 1
explanation: Compare wages, prices, all bilateral share ratios, and real wages. The final decision also requires all three convergence flags.

title: 05 · Apply both strict bounds
explanation: The denominator is the levels-route ratio, not the change minus one. The two error tests are separate, so one cannot compensate for the other.

title: 06 · Record evidence
equation: PASS = converged(E0,E1,hats) AND every comparison passes
explanation: The builder runs this exact verification routine, embeds its certificate, and hashes the reviewed source. A completed run is not itself a pass.
